title: Pieter Battier to Gaspar Fagel, Madrid, 1686–1688

steps.what: De Leeuw 2000 describes Fagel codebooks, not Battier; no edition found; letters absent from DECODE.
Named Battier key NA 1.10.29 inv. 1209, DECODE R2794; old 5345 citation corrected.
Letter table and about 1400 codebook values transcribed; marked cipher tokens and inventory retained.
Key applied to five focus letters and supporting letters; the earlier volume estimate was roughly 55%, with no revised denominator for the 235-token addition.

First two validation letters: 1113/1132 comparable tokens agree (98.3%); 94.7% key-alone; 18 positions not comparable. Third validation: 19 December 1686, four passages and 186 tokens, reproduces the contemporary list on 32R apart from spelling and gedaan/afgedaen. Confirms 15:325 = wat and 12:409 = syn; strengthens the identification of inv. 1209 as Battier's key. Comparison is not blind.
300-permutation control: 72% spelled runs segment into Dutch, mean 1.2%, maximum 4.1% shuffled.

Codex software re-decoding, not paleography: 19 Dec 186/186 is validation of contemporary plaintext; 24 April 1687 passes strict sense without a known contemporary decipherment, 230/235 (97.9%), as does 8 April 1688, 313/323 (96.9%), conservatively 312/323 (96.6%). Dec 1687 94.3% and Feb 1688 92.3% do not pass.

WAINUT (PR #65): folder key applied to scan 67R cipher lines 1-3 (June 1687, listed as not read): 45 tokens, 21 letters and 24 codes, 8 code rows looked up in the key scans; grades H 41, M 3, I 1 (885 open). Gastañaga's expenses and 'soigneuslyke borse' to the 'totale ruïne' of the Spanish Netherlands. Key-rotated-by-one control loses the sense (weak for codes). Key row correction: 11:718 soetjens, 11:719 soetelaars (key s59L1); neither occurs in tokens/.

WAINUT (PR #65): single Gemini pass against this folder's checked tokens: same number 88% (58R) / 95% (59L) but same decoded value only 71% / 78%, so no machine-only transcription is offered as a reading.

WAINUT (PR #67): folder key applied to seven 1687 letters listed as not read: 16 Jan (207 groups, 11 uncertain), 13 Feb (272/11), 27 Feb (575/8), 13 Mar 55L only (66/1), 10 Jun 67R (152/6), 20 Nov (60/1), 18 Dec 94R ll. 1-5 (57/1); 1,389 groups, 39 uncertain, every group checked by eye on the scans. Codes from key/dict 586, letters 645, and 158 from an unchecked machine read of the code book (wainut/r24_1687/key_rows_machine.tsv). Each letter beats 20 row-shifted and 200 shuffled keys under a Dutch 4-gram model (control script not included). The 2 Jan 1687 letter (35R, 36L) has heavy interlinear decipherment: inv/orch_letters.tsv was wrong to list it as 'no'.

Review of PR #65 and #67 (Bourdeau with Claude Opus 5.5): check_67R.py and check_1687.py re-run, counts reproduced (1,389 groups, 39 uncertain; dict 586, letter 645, rows 158). The 158 machine-read key rows are not yet eye-checked and the 4-gram control is not reproducible from the repository, so the seven letters stay contributed readings in wainut/ and are not counted in fraction_read. inv/orch_letters.tsv updated for 2 Jan 1687 and the seven letters.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked, per letter, Feyseel Nur's tokens/<date>_groups.txt and per-scan token files and the readings/s*_text.txt key readings, with the transcribed contemporary decipherments (28R, 42R-43R) beside the letters they validate; WAINUT's eight contributed 1687 passages (wainut/) are not profile documents and are not listed.

outcome.method_basis: The contemporary key explicitly names Battier; NA 1.10.29 inv. 1209 / DECODE R2794 was applied to his correspondence. The third validation against scan 32R strengthens this identification.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Earlier volume estimate, about 55% of cipher in inv. 401; no revised volume-wide denominator after adding 235 tokens from 24 April 1687. Inventory: inv/orch_letters.tsv and inv/nw.tsv. Strict results: codex_review/metrics.tsv and codex_review/review_1687-04-24.md.

gaps.detail: Surplus 8=e (possible encipherment slip); 5:623 gra[tie] partly covered in the key; gehelyk, sedert dat and soo als hy; exact condition of Gastanaga's departure. Five excluded positions: codex_review/review_1687-04-24.md.
12:6?0; getwist versus Turck(en); Novelli/Hofmeester; gesoubconneert gouverneren; Sex.; names, 81 and other repairs: codex_review/semantic_adjustments.tsv.

gaps.detail: Not yet transcribed; workable with the same key. No claim that all possible research has been exhausted.

gaps.detail: No check for nearby separate decipherment sheets has been made.

gaps.detail: 158 code values from an unchecked machine read of the key (wainut/r24_1687/key_rows_machine.tsv) need an eye check; 54R, 55R, 67L and the rest of 93R-95L are not read; 4-gram control script not supplied

outcome.notes: Two letters pass strict sense without a known contemporary decipherment: 24 April 1687, 230/235 (97.9%) conservatively; 8 April 1688, 313/323 (96.9%), conservatively 312/323 (96.6%). The 19 December 1686 letter, 186/186, is the third validation against contemporary plaintext on 32R, not a new reading. Others 199/211 and 250/271 are below. No aggregate grade conversion or volume-wide coherent fraction is claimed. Legacy reading grades remain unchanged; 12:409 = syn is now confirmed by contemporary plaintext. 81=e is contextual and absent from all three validation letters.

credits.note: PR #22: Battier 1686-88 letters read with the named key NA 1.10.29 inv. 1209 (with Claude and Codex)
contemporary key naming Battier (NA 1.10.29 inv. 1209, DECODE R2794) and the decipherments on scans 28R, 32R, 42R-43R, 101R
PR #65 and #67: folder key applied to eight 1687 passages (1,389 groups); key row 11:718/719 and the 2 Jan 1687 inventory line corrected

texts.label: 5 Dec 1686 (scans 30R, 31L)
texts.summary: Battier, Dutch envoy extraordinary in Madrid, to Grand Pensionary Gaspar Fagel; a contemporary decipherment survives on scan 28R and is transcribed beside the key reading as a validation.

texts.label: 19 Dec 1686 (scans 31R, 32L)
texts.summary: Battier to Fagel; the four numbered passages deciphered by a contemporary clerk on scan 32R make this letter the third validation of the key against contemporary plaintext.

texts.label: 30 Jan 1687 (scans 41R, 42L, 44R)
texts.summary: Battier to Fagel; the contemporary decipherment on scans 42R-43R (file misdated 16 Jan) deciphers this one letter and is transcribed beside the key reading.

texts.label: 24 Apr 1687 (scans 58R, 59L)
texts.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid, with no known contemporary decipherment: Gastanaga may be removed before the end of his three years or employed in Peru or Catalonia; the Emperor's ambassador moves heaven and earth to regain the Queen's good grace, working through a nun, the confessor and ministers, but Battier thinks the Queen will never forget the harm he did her.

texts.label: 4 Dec 1687 (scans 91R, 92L)
texts.summary: Battier to Fagel; the clear close on 92R reports that Leganés wants service and lodging money for 14 men and that the Prince of Parma has arrived with a train of 140 persons.

texts.label: 29 Jan 1688 (scan 97R)
texts.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid; no contemporary decipherment recorded.

texts.label: 12 Feb 1688 (scans 99R, 100R)
texts.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid; separate decipherment sheets near this letter have not been checked.

texts.label: 26 Feb 1688 (scan 101R)
texts.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid, partly deciphered interlinear at the time (scan 101R).

texts.label: 8 Apr 1688 (scans 107R-109L)
texts.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid, with no contemporary decipherment: the Grand Maestre has ordered his agent to reassure the old Queen, and a sworn party forms against him (the Constable of Castile, Os[t]una and Monterey?); the reviewed reconstruction (codex_review/april_reading.md) supersedes the earlier fluent reading.

prior.where: Contemporary decipherments on inv. 401 scans 28R, 32R (19 December 1686, four numbered passages), 42R–43R and 101R; no edition found in the prior-art search.

human: Decipherment by Feyseel Nur with Claude and Codex; original division of transcription work undocumented.
